minutes.headline: Water district voters approved the Hickory Hills well pilot study article after a recount, 79 to 77.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District meeting took up one article: appropriating money from the water system enhancement account to hire Tighe & Bond for a pilot study of treating iron, manganese and PFAS at the Hickory Hills well. Residents, especially from Hickory Hills, pressed on lake levels, scope, cost and need. A late amendment was refused as discussion was closed. A standing vote was tied, a recount gave 79 to 77, and the article passed.

what_happened.line: Water district voters passed the Hickory Hills well pilot study article after a recount, 79 to 77 as heard, following a tied standing count.
The article draws on the water system enhancement account to hire Tighe & Bond to design and coordinate a pilot study of iron, manganese and PFAS treatment.
The moderator closed discussion and declined a late amendment that would have required the Hickory Hills board's conditions, including a hydrogeologist for lake level.
Commissioners said the Hickory Hills board could see and comment on the study scope before the project goes out.
Commissioners said funding is available only for wells above allowable limits, so only Hickory Hills qualifies; otherwise costs fall on water rates.

why_it_matters: The study is a first step toward treating the well, and a commissioner could not give a treatment cost, so a later spending request for a plant could come before water district voters.
If grant money is not available for the work, the cost would fall on water rates, which water district customers pay.
Residents near Hickory Hills raised lake level and scope, and the scope was not put in writing before the vote.
watch_next: The written study scope, which commissioners said the Hickory Hills board could review before the project goes out.
Any later water district article asking for money to treat the well or build a plant, which the study is meant to price.
